claims.statement: TFM and TFI own native UI, adapters, composition and lifecycle; non-presentation shared modules cannot import either app or AppKit/UIKit/IOKit/ServiceManagement, while TermindPresentation has a separate, broader import ban on implementation/storage frameworks and app/platform modules. Application and Persistence have additional directional dependency exclusions, and source tests enforce only their listed imports and token checks.

TermindPersistence exclusively owns SwiftData models, historical schemas, migrations, and container construction, and the app composition roots retain one container per process rather than silently replacing a failed persistent store.

Desktop AppModel coordinates process services while WindowModel owns navigation and live Workspaces. MobileAppModel owns process services, process-local recently closed records and the session registry; MobileWorkspaceSessionModel owns scene-local ordered live Workspaces and in-memory connection-intent descriptors. MobileSceneModel owns navigation using mutually exclusive Workspace/Transfers destinations and Connection Picker/Batch Startup sheets.

SSH connection attempts use one-shot wipeable secret ownership, and interaction-forbidden auxiliary connections reject trust, passphrase, user-presence, and keyboard-interactive work rather than retaining interactive secret material.

SFTP transfer runtime is process-local and coordinates bounded fair admission, connection/channel topology, resumable temporary files, conflict policy, direct remote copy, and external-edit version checks without persisting live connection state.
AgentKit remains the host-neutral runtime boundary while Termind registers host-aware tools, persistence, policy, remote interaction, and native presentation around it.

Vault, Connection History, Device, Settings and Metrics own separate lifecycle and journal state; History and Device share the deployed zone and HistoryRecordSyncCoordinator implementation but not engines, subscriptions, safety consumer or enablement. Vault and Device follow master iCloud while History is optional, and completed current-engine fetches gate uploads.

Mobile startup retires mobile.workspaces.v1 and mobile.recentlyClosed.v2 without decoding, migration or replacement storage, preserving unrelated defaults. Relaunch has no Workspaces or recently closed records even when Hosts survive; dormant/reopen state is process-local. Separate explicit validated Live Activity recovery rebuilds a saved-Host Workspace with a new ID and remote-session selection required and deduplicates repeated cross-scene links; stale ID-only, deleted-Host, unsupported or command-bearing links cannot guess a connection.

The current SwiftData schema is V54. V51 adds Snippet colors, V52 removes retired keyword-highlighting preferences, V53 replaces the Host backing with session-persistence and agent-forwarding fields, and V54 replaces it with icon-override support; these transitions are lightweight with historical model shapes retained. Local schema and CloudKit envelope versions are independent; Snippets read V1/V2, write V2 and reject colored V1 encoding.

Shared CloudSyncLifecycleSafety and CloudSyncSafetyStore persist scoped unsupported/unreadable record restrictions; decoding quarantines full native-field records, and journals, restored engine queues, batches and providers exclude blocked uploads while retaining pending intent. A successful supported reconciliation clears the restriction atomically; retries and restarts cannot bypass it and other records continue syncing.

Connection history synchronizes saved-host SSH/Telnet/SFTP events with stable source-device ID, start time and optional end time. A separate synchronized device directory resolves mutable display names; retained events are capped at 250 and all-device History presentation at 100 on desktop and 50 on mobile.

Terminal font family, size and follow-theme-size stay device-local; shared binding-driven controls use an 8–36 editing range with a macOS slider and iOS stepper, while app-owned catalogs include families with any loadable monospaced member and sort using the current locale.

Unavailable and wrong-appearance saved theme names remain in preferences and the displayed summary without appearance-time persistence, though they do not appear as selectable tiles among available themes. Both apps use shared filtered and sorted options with a fallback notice; rendering applies the appearance default, custom commands, then local typography.

AssistantExecutionController captures turn content and configuration synchronously before memory or compaction awaits, after optional model-selection persistence. Output, selections and file contents require explicit payload-carrying ContextChips; detach removes payload and accepted capture consumes attachments once. Full composed extraction and images remain in replay while bubbles render authored text or legacy visiblePrompt and attachment references. Original non-image bytes support reopening, not model input; legacy file references fall back to extracted text.

While an Assistant capture is preparing, cancellation makes its identity noncurrent synchronously and joins tracked edit/history and preparation work before attempting an interrupted save; interruption is projected only on successful save, whereas stop alone does not await it. In the separate savingFailure phase cancellation joins the existing failed-snapshot save rather than replacing it with interruption; archive/delete wait, manual compaction refuses active preparation, and selection changes do not cancel it.

History edits commit before live replacement, truncate at the selected user message in canonical run/message order, preserve the same-run prefix and its owned tool graph with a neutral completed summary, and prune compactions by removed message boundaries while considering compacted display history for live ownership and title retention.

A successfully edited message starts in a same-message-ID staging run; the first real saved snapshot reassigns only that staged row and removes staging while preserving chronology and old replay ownership. Live running, interrupted, and failed-run adoption uses the same guarded provenance; missing-model/credential preparation failures hold the preparation until their asynchronous save commits before projecting failure, and failed saves report an error without adopting staging. Repository-instance retired IDs reject late writes.

Saved-Host deletion commits a pending marker and ordered outbox jobs with the repository mutation before hiding the Host from snapshots; ordered cleanup closes runtime Workspaces, cancels transfers, stops forwarding, clears references/history and finally removes the Host and its owned Identities, while independent Known Hosts trust survives.

Mobile local Host deletion proactively disconnects Assistant, requests closure of live/dormant Workspaces, forgets closed recovery records and invalidates edits/transfers/forwardings/Metrics before durable deletion and outbox start; managed-session closure may defer removal through authorization. Desktop requests durable deletion before projecting removal and clearing history, with runtime callbacks/outbox cleanup. Mobile closure requests do not guarantee immediate remote-session termination or restoration on durable-request failure.

On mobile all-scenes background pauses sync, Metrics and outbox before a finite background task; only expiration suspends Workspace transports, stops forwardings, pauses transfers and expires Assistant work. Foreground resumes eligible existing Workspaces and process services, while failed initial selection needs explicit retry.

ArchitectureBoundaryTests scan direct Swift files in the Cloud directory whose text contains the specified CKSyncEngineDelegate declaration for lifecycle batching/upload/handling and remote decoding/quarantine tokens, without a legacy read-only History exception. Other source scans constrain AppStrings and SwiftData ownership; these syntactic checks do not prove runtime behavior or cover differently declared or nested delegates.

AgentToolPresentation creates an approval-only projection of in-memory original arguments without attaching it to durable cards; it can replace host_id with a resolved host name and use an injected presenter for the remaining reviewable arguments, keeping long argument values out of the short action title.

AgentToolPresentation renders local built-in result detail through decoded JSON and an injectable presenter or generic formatter but retains MCP's remote-defined JSON presentation; unsuccessful knowledge results cannot select success detail, and duplicate denial reasons are suppressed from the result detail.

Assistant tool batch summary groups calls by tool identity, terminal state and knowledge action so mixed failures remain visible; bounded head/tail previews limit rendered output to 8,192 characters and 120 lines by default while preserving the full transformed text for Copy.

MobileBackgroundController invokes UIKit expiration synchronously on the MainActor before retiring a finite background task lease; it ignores stale callbacks, ends valid leases at most once even if expiration reenters begin, and invokes expiration for an invalid returned task without ending that invalid identifier.

When the last mobile scene enters background MobileAppModel pauses sync, metrics, edits and outbox, then starts a background lease; expiration synchronously requests Workspace suspension, forwarding stop, transfer pause and Assistant expiration, without waiting for asynchronous Assistant persistence or transport drains.

MobileAssistantModel expiration fences new Assistant work while suspending, requests cancellation of captured preparations and all stored conversations before awaiting any conversation drain, then closes background commands and Agent connections; focused tests cover blocked sends, edits, plan implementation and ordering against blocked saves.

Desktop termination gates cleanup on application-scoped Workspace confirmation and dirty-edit recheck, distinct from pane close and window vetoes. Idempotent shutdown fences Assistant admission, cancels preparations and stops conversations before drains, stops MCP/SFTP concurrently and closes Agent resources after drains. Native window dismissal disconnects clients preserving remote-session recovery and Quit uses applicationTermination: only explicitClose ends managed attachments. RemoteSessionCloseCoordinator skips unmanaged references, deduplicates identity, terminates without initial confirmation and on failure offers retry, Cancel or Disconnect Only; failure alone cannot authorize removal, retry retains partial progress and cancellation generations fence late results.

The macOS termination delegate replies exactly once after either asynchronous app cleanup completes or a three-second fallback timeout; the timeout limits the quit wait rather than guaranteeing completion of persistence.

App-facing copy, including single-platform wording, is defined as LocalizedStringResource entries under TermindPresentation/Strings using AppStrings for both apps to reuse, with protocol values, identifiers and diagnostic codes excluded; catalog entries remain in shared Resources.

The SwiftSyntax AppStrings checker flags selected user-facing literal forms in TFM and TFI and complements the current Python localization checker; contributor guidance still names retired check-zh-localization.sh rather than current check-localization.py. These checks do not comprehensively verify every UI string or displayed translation.

Pane title drags and native Workspace List drags on macOS 26 and later can request a new window for an unaccepted, uncancelled release outside the source window; live ownership remains in the source until the native destination registers.

The macOS app is its own XCTest host: DEBUG test detection uses an in-memory SwiftData container, suppresses automatic windows and restoration for ordinary tests, and requires an explicit visible-window opt-in for tests that show windows or take focus.
The mobile app runs its real scene with testing dependencies under XCTest, while mobile key-window integration suites require explicit opt-in and disabled parallel testing.

Both shared app string catalogs remain manually maintained, requiring explicit keys and Chinese translations and canonical Xcode-compatible formatting; single-target stale flags do not justify deleting keys. Both project configurations disable generated catalog symbols. The project defaults are Swift 6.0, approachable concurrency, complete strict concurrency, ExistentialAny, MainActor isolation and Swift warnings-as-errors; apps, shared frameworks and tests inherit the isolation default, widgets restate it, and the MCP bridge and forwarding benchmark override it with nonisolated and -parse-as-library. TFMTests only relaxes imported deprecated-declaration diagnostics through -Xcc. Apps enable localization-string emission while all six shared frameworks, FrameworkTests and TFITests disable it. Debug enables testability and -Onone, while Release uses whole-module compilation and disables assertions. TermindWidgets is an iOS/iPadOS extension with extension-only APIs and TFIWidgets-owned source and metadata.

Localization checks complement rendering coverage: SwiftSyntax flags selected UI literals; check-localization.py validates canonical manual catalogs, finished zh-Hans/zh-Hant/ja/ko/de/fr translations, positional argument types and percents, plural branches and Chinese/Japanese spacing. Plurals require other-only for Chinese/Japanese/Korean, one/other for German, and one/other with optional many for French. Path-filtered Ubuntu CI runs normalizer/localization unit tests and the Python checker on pull requests and main pushes, not native rendering or SwiftSyntax copy checks.

History and Device use version-gated native-field ConnectionHistoryItem and DeviceItem records in their shared deployed zone; HistorySyncPersistence prepares native local events and devices rather than running the retired Vault-to-History importer, and capability checkpoint changes force scoped refetch before the new checkpoint is committed after a successful fetch.

DeviceDirectoryModel registers the local installation when absent, caches repository reads, invalidates the cache after reload or a successful rename, and reports storage failures without changing the displayed current name on a failed rename.

Shared sync batching rejects unjournaled or blocked mutations, deduplicates record IDs, and limits the combined save/delete request to 250; it persists the delete handoff before transmission, does not hand off concurrent operations for the same in-flight deleted ID, and cannot acknowledge a delete after that record has been reobserved.
Desktop startup fails rather than replacing a failed persistent SwiftData store; iOS retains a failed startup result and displays a store-open error scene instead of instantiating another store.

Mobile native-session reconciliation transfers orphaned live Workspaces, order and unread state in process to an active owner without reconnecting, creating history or saving ownership to disk; without a recipient it waits. Scene disconnection alone does not discard ownership. A late native discard removes the original window's entries even after handoff and records a grouped recently closed window.

The architecture source scans reject dialog titles that bridge LocalizedStringResource to .swiftUIKey for alert or confirmationDialog instead of passing the resource directly; this syntactic check is not a runtime localization proof.

NotificationPreferences is a Settings-synchronized notification record introduced in V41: independent Assistant, terminal and SFTP modes default to unfocused with system terminal delivery and a five-second threshold; edits validate and persist before publishing, remote updates do not echo, and failed loads suppress initial permission requests rather than using fallback defaults. Initial system authorization is requested at most once per model instance, only if a category requires system delivery; selecting terminal bell avoids the request only if Assistant and SFTP system modes are also off or notifications are disabled.

TerminalCommandMonitor owns per-live-terminal unread completions and accepts shell-integration or fallback OSC 133 completion independently of views/history; delivery requires focus and duration policy, while the app-injected coordinator selects bell or system notification and rechecks policy and target existence on send.

SFTP notifications aggregate terminal results until no queued or running transfers remain; paused/cancelled transfers do not delay a batch and resumed transfers start new work, with delivery policy rechecked at enqueue time.

App-owned Assistant notification observation deduplicates run-completion and pending-interaction notifications even when focus suppresses delivery, retires obsolete interaction notifications, and marks invisible conversations unread; badges observe live unread state instead of persisting notification counts.

SystemNotifications gates dispatch on authorization and a caller-provided currentness predicate before enqueueing and removes requests made obsolete during the send; it encodes notification target kind/ID for platform routing and defers clicks received before a router is attached. Desktop restores Assistant history before routing while mobile activates the existing owning scene and drops missing terminal targets rather than starting a new connection.

History editing permits removal of executed tool history: truncation atomically deletes suffix-owned invocation, result and review rows while preserving prefix-owned work; legacy invocations without recoverable source or call ownership belong to the suffix at or after the edit boundary. Selected user messages with agent-message provenance remain ineligible for editing; transcript truncation does not undo remote tool effects.

Approval projection for local chat-collaboration tools renders only arguments chosen by the injected presenter, or no arguments if it is unavailable; collaboration result cards use presenter-selected fields or a safe unavailable-details fallback rather than exposing raw JSON. Local pane read/list transcript details likewise expose pane metadata instead of terminal output, including on restored cards.

CloudSyncLifecycle detaches scheduled synchronization operations and engine cancellation from CloudKit delegate task-local context, while retaining MainActor isolation; regression tests cover start, retry, local-change callbacks and account-change cancellation.

CloudKit ordinary zone deletion resets and requeues scoped journal records and recreates the zone, whereas a purge or encrypted-data reset retires the engine and purges the scoped cloud cache without recreating the zone during that event; a subsequent explicit local write can start a new engine.

Within a fetched CloudKit batch, if any included representation of a record name fails decoding, that name is quarantined and even other successfully decoded representations of the same name are excluded from the applied batch.

On macOS, persistent container construction acquires a nonblocking exclusive lock on a stable store-adjacent file before SwiftData opens or migrates; same-process containers for the canonical store URL share the lease until the last closes, while another process is refused without mutating the store, and forced exit releases the lock without unlinking its file.

Before opening the macOS persistent store, startup checks for other running instances with the same bundle identifier to protect against older app versions lacking the store lock; a store-in-use failure presents an alert and exits, whereas other store-opening failures terminate startup rather than falling back to memory.

Production Pro access is mediated by RevenueCat: the live controller uses bundled configuration to create the purchase service; that service configures anonymous StoreKit 2 RevenueCat, observes customer-info updates, fetches current info, uses cached info on network failure, and conditionally synchronizes pre-integration purchases once rather than running a separate StoreKit transaction observer.

Only the configured verified RevenueCat entitlement grants production Pro: active lifetime, trial, subscription and grace grant access subject to their deadline, whereas failed verification, billing retry, expiration or revocation do not. The controller preserves previously resolved access on a failed refresh, prioritizes newer customer-info updates over stale refreshes, and schedules an expiration refresh.
Command history belongs to one live terminal session, retains at most 250 entries in memory, retains its completed snapshot over disconnect/reconnect, and clears permanently when closed.

TerminalFindController dismissal is idempotent and query-preserving: active dismissal emits end and clears presentation, default dismissal restores terminal focus, and restoringFocus: false suppresses that request. Reopening restarts a retained nonempty query unless resize-suspended; resize resume only restarts a still-presented nonempty query.

TerminalFindController dispatches search only for changed query values when not resize-suspended and permits navigation only while presented with a nonempty query and no suspension. Resize suspension retains UI/query state, and resume searches the latest query rather than a captured earlier value.

Mobile native search owns responder dismissal: the Workspace presentation binding dismisses shared Find without terminal focus restoration, and the native search adapter fences synchronization, text changes and new presentation during dismissal so Cancel preserves the query or SFTP filter rather than reopening search through model feedback.

MobileWorkspaceView keeps SSH/Telnet terminal surfaces mounted beneath Journey/authentication/host-key overlays, hiding and disabling covered content instead of replacing it. The native search modifier remains on stable Workspace chrome outside that connection-state branch, including SFTP Journey presentation.

MobileTerminalSearchIntegrationTests is an opt-in serialized key-window suite covering repeated native and programmatic dismissal with retained terminal queries, repeated SFTP filter reopening, and search-host identity across Journey for SSH/SFTP; terminal identity is asserted for SSH, not a Telnet-specific integration case.

RemoteCharsetStreamConverter preserves stream continuity: valid bytes convert, malformed/unrepresentable bytes pass through verbatim, incomplete bytes buffer and flush unchanged, and unavailable iconv preserves raw bytes. The legacy recovery parameter no longer rejects input. Value APIs use this converter and String(decoding:as:), so invalid UTF-8 can become display replacements rather than strict conversion failure; Serial also emits converted/trailing data.
